title: Picking a cuisine filter crashes the page
scenario: You are on the Zomato restaurant discovery team. The restaurant service occasionally returns an error for specific cuisine filters, and the page needs to handle that gracefully.
symptom: Selecting the Italian cuisine filter breaks the page — the restaurant grid disappears and the app stops responding, instead of showing a message that the restaurant list could not be loaded.
hints: Select the Italian filter and watch the console/crash panel — what exactly is undefined when the crash happens?
useRestaurants.js calls res.json() and trusts the result is always a restaurant list. Is that true for every HTTP status code?

There's an ErrorBanner component already built and imported nowhere — useRestaurants needs to expose an error state, and RestaurantGrid needs to render it instead of mapping over restaurants unconditionally.

rubric.description: useRestaurants checks the response status (e.g. response.ok, or a status outside 200–299) before treating the body as a successful restaurant list, instead of always reading body.restaurants.
Selecting the Italian cuisine filter, for which GET /api/restaurants returns a 503, shows a visible error message to the user instead of a blank grid or a crash.

The error state is driven by the real response status or body from GET /api/restaurants, not by a hardcoded check for the Italian cuisine specifically (e.g. `if (cuisine === 'italian')`) that fakes the error message without inspecting the response.
Selecting a cuisine filter the mock returns 200 for still shows that cuisine's restaurant list correctly.
